h1: The 7 Best Printers for Windows 11 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Printers for Windows 11: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 printers for Windows 11, scored on driver support, document feeders and connectivity, from Brother and Canon to Epson and HP.
summary: The Brother DCP-L2640DW is the safest printer for Windows 11: a monochrome laser with a full driver package, duplex and wireless. On a budget, the Canon PIXMA TR4720 includes a document feeder. For the lowest cost per page, the Epson EcoTank ET-2800 refills from bottles. And for a shared wired office, the EcoTank ET-4800 adds Ethernet and a feeder.
intro: Windows 11 will happily install a basic driver for almost any printer on its own, which is exactly the problem. The generic driver prints, but it hides scan tools, quality settings and maintenance utilities that only the maker's full driver package gives you.

So this ranking looks at what a printer actually brings to a Windows 11 PC: a full driver and utility set, a feeder if you scan paperwork, wired or wireless connectivity, and running costs. We reviewed seven current models and scored them on the Primea framework.

products.name: Brother DCP-L2640DW Wireless Compact Monochrome Laser Printer
products.verdict: A compact laser with a full Windows 11 driver, scan tools, duplex and wireless.
products.description:
The DCP-L2640DW is a black and white laser, and Brother's own driver for Windows 11 brings scanning, copying and upkeep utilities that the built-in driver never shows. Automatic duplex printing and wireless connectivity are included, in a compact body.

It ranks first because laser printers rarely suffer the clogged-nozzle and offline problems that trouble inkjets on a PC left idle. The tradeoff is colour: it prints black and white only, so the Epson and Canon inkjets here win for photos.

Best for a Windows 11 home office that prints mostly documents and wants reliability.
products.idealFor: Home offices printing mostly text documents.
products.skipIf: You need colour or photo prints.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TR4720 All-in-One Wireless Printer
products.verdict: Colour all-in-one with an auto document feeder, fax and Canon's full Windows driver.
products.description:
The TR4720 installs Canon's full driver on Windows 11, which adds scan and print quality settings beyond the basic driver. It includes an auto document feeder, handy for scanning a stack of pages without placing each sheet by hand, along with fax and wireless printing.

It ranks second because it is an inkjet that uses cartridges, so running cost per page is higher than the EcoTank. The feeder and colour are the reasons to choose it over the Brother.

Good for students and small home offices who scan paperwork and need colour.
cons: Cartridge ink costs more per page
products.idealFor: Students and small offices that scan paperwork.
products.skipIf: You print a lot and want the lowest page cost.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-2800 Wireless Color All-in-One
products.verdict: Refillable ink tanks and the Epson Scan 2 utility for regular Windows 11 printing.
products.description:
The ET-2800 replaces cartridges with refillable ink tanks, which cuts the cost of each page for a Windows 11 home office that prints often. Epson's complete driver adds the Epson Scan 2 utility and print quality controls, and startup ink bottles are included.

It does not have a feeder, so scanning is one flatbed sheet at a time, which is why the Canon TR4720 beats it for paperwork. Where it wins is running cost, which adds up over a year of printing.

Best for regular colour printing where cost per page matters more than document scanning.
products.idealFor: Regular colour printing on a budget over time.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-4800 Wireless All-in-One with ADF and Ethernet
products.verdict: Feeder, Ethernet and fax on top of a tank system. Stable for shared Windows 11 PCs.
products.description:
The ET-4800 adds a document feeder and Ethernet to the EcoTank line, both useful in a Windows 11 office where several PCs might share one printer over a wired network. Ethernet is less prone to the offline errors that wireless connections can show after a PC wakes from sleep.

It ranks fourth because it costs more than the ET-2800, and many homes do not need a feeder or fax. If you do, it is the one to buy here.

Best for offices that share a printer between several PCs and scan paperwork regularly.

products.name: Brother Work Smart 1360 Wireless Color Inkjet All-in-One
products.verdict: Colour inkjet with automatic duplex and Brother's full Windows 11 driver.
products.description:
For the Work Smart 1360, Brother's complete Windows 11 driver supplies duplex settings and status monitoring that the stock install lacks. Automatic duplex printing saves paper on longer documents, and a 1.8 inch colour display handles basic settings. A Refresh Subscription ink trial is included, which is optional.

It ranks fifth because it is a cartridge inkjet and there is no feeder, so it neither beats the DCP-L2640DW on reliability nor the EcoTanks on running cost. Choose it for colour with duplex from a brand whose drivers are well behaved.

A fit for home users who print long colour documents.
products.idealFor: Home users printing long colour documents.

products.name: HP DeskJet 4355 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: HP Smart app setup and monitoring, with a 3-month Instant Ink trial included.
products.description:
Setup, job tracking and phone scanning for the DeskJet 4355 all run through the HP Smart app. Should it ever appear offline, try the Windows 11 printer troubleshooter before blaming the hardware, because that often clears it.

It ranks sixth because it is a basic flatbed with no feeder, and HP's Instant Ink trial is an enrolment you should read carefully before accepting, since it is a subscription. Its draw is how easy it is to get running.

Pick it for light home printing where easy setup matters more than features.
cons: Instant Ink trial is a subscription
products.idealFor: Light home printing with easy setup.
products.skipIf: You want to avoid ink subscriptions.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS5320 All-in-One Wireless Printer
products.verdict: Five individual ink tanks and Canon's full Windows 11 driver in a compact body.
products.description:
Canon's complete Windows 11 driver for the TS5320 opens up print quality levels, tray options and scan settings that the basic driver keeps out of sight. Its five-colour individual ink system lets you replace one depleted colour without discarding a combined cartridge, and it supports AirPrint.

It ranks last because it is the oldest design here with no feeder and no duplex noted. For a photo-leaning household with a small desk, the separate inks are a real saving.

Best for compact desks where photo printing matters and paperwork scanning does not.

whatMatters.detail: Windows 11 can install a basic driver automatically that prints but hides scan, copy and maintenance tools. Download the maker's full driver package from their site after setup. Check the listing for a full driver package mention before ordering.

Wireless is convenient but can show an offline state when the printer sleeps or the router changes. Ethernet is steadier for shared use. If more than two PCs print to it, look for an Ethernet port in the specs.

A flatbed scans one page at a time. An automatic document feeder scans a stack unattended. If you scan contracts, tax forms or school paperwork, a feeder is worth paying for. Look for ADF in the title or bullets.
Tank printers cost less per page but more upfront. Cartridge printers are cheaper to buy but costlier to run. Estimate your monthly pages: under 100 favours a laser or cheap inkjet, over that a tank.

Some listings include a trial of a manufacturer ink subscription. It is optional, but read the terms before enrolling, because it can bill after the trial. Look for Instant Ink or Refresh in the listing.

faq.q: Does Windows 11 install printer drivers automatically?
faq.a: It installs a basic driver for most printers. For scan tools, quality settings and maintenance, download the full driver package from the maker, as on the Brother, Canon and Epson models here.

faq.q: Why does my printer show offline in Windows 11?
faq.a: Common causes are a sleeping printer, a Wi-Fi change or a stuck queue. Run the Windows printer troubleshooter first. An Ethernet connection, like the Epson ET-4800, is less prone to it.

faq.q: Is the Brother DCP-L2640DW worth it over an inkjet?
faq.a: If you print mostly black text, yes. Toner does not dry out, so it suits irregular printing. For colour or photos, choose an Epson or Canon inkjet instead.

faq.q: Do I need a document feeder?
faq.a: Only if you scan stacks of paper. The Canon TR4720 and Epson ET-4800 have one. For single pages, a flatbed such as the ET-2800 is fine.

faq.q: Should I accept the Instant Ink or Refresh trial?
faq.a: Only if you read the terms. They are optional subscriptions that can start billing after the trial. Skip them if you want to avoid recurring charges.

faq.q: Can I print from my phone to these?
faq.a: Yes. The HP DeskJet 4355 uses the HP Smart app, and the Canon TS5320 supports AirPrint. The others offer mobile printing through their own apps.

finalTake: For most Windows 11 users the Brother DCP-L2640DW is the right buy: a full driver, duplex and a laser that stays ready. On a budget, the Canon PIXMA TR4720 adds a document feeder. For the lowest page cost, the Epson EcoTank ET-2800 refills from bottles. And for a shared office, the EcoTank ET-4800 gives you Ethernet and a feeder.
